new.analysis:
## What the week was
The three planned walk-runs on Mon Sep 21, Wed Sep 23 and Sat Sep 26 did not happen, and no run was logged at all. The rest days were kept only because nothing was run, so there was no overrun and no session to correct.

## The last five weeks
Two weeks ago you completed all three runs, so the gap is not a fitness problem. The week of Sep 7 – 13 was cut short by the cold and fever, and this week the gap has no stated reason.

| Week of | Runs | Distance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aug 24 – 30 | 3 | 6.78 km |
| Aug 31 – Sep 6 | 3 | 7.30 km |
| Sep 7 – 13 | 1 | 2.78 km |
| Sep 14 – 20 | 3 | 6.98 km |
| Sep 21 – 27 | 0 | 0 km |

## What the check-in says
Your sleep was 7.5 hours, stress was low, and you wrote that your body feels all good. That does not suggest tiredness or illness, so the zero runs need an explanation from you. If the runs happened but did not reach Tempo, tell me, because that changes this read.

## Why this plan
After a gap, the first run should feel like one you have done before, so Monday repeats the structure from two weeks ago. The build phase calls for firmer work, but starting hard after a missed week is the wrong order. Wednesday is the only firmer session, and Saturday moves to 3-minute running blocks so that continuous running starts to grow.

Easy runs stay under 145 beats per minute, and the firmer session stays between 150 and 158, well under your maximum of 182. This week is already light because it restarts the routine, so it needs no extra easing.

## Realism for November
Finishing the 5K without a walk means about 40 minutes of continuous running at an easy pace, a long step from 2-minute blocks. It is possible in six weeks only if three runs happen every week and the running blocks grow each week. If that does not happen, I will say so and we will set a realistic target together.
